title: Type III CRISPR-Cas systems preferentially acquire spacers from early-expressed phage genes in a transcription-dependent manner.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded and unpacked the full supplement (4.5 MB inner zip): one Word file and one Excel file. Parsed all 6 Word tables: 30 + 22 + 130 = 182 individual BIM (bacteriophage-insensitive mutant) spacer sequences with a gene target and strand, 37 escaper-phage rows, 7 deletion rows, 66 PCR primers. Opened the Excel growth-curve file: 4 sheets, 245-929 time rows, 141-321 columns, 39 distinct strain labels in total. Queried NCBI BioProject, NCBI SRA (esearch), the NCBI BioProject web page and the ENA (European Nucleotide Archive) mirror for PRJNA1379557: all four returned zero records or an error page on 2026-10-16.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: That high-throughput spacer sequencing was done, that spacers were aligned with bowtie and turned into per-position depth tracks normalised as SPM (spacers per million), the 752 Streptococcus phage genomes used as the alignment database, and the natural-spacer survey of all S. thermophilus assemblies. None of these processed tables or tracks appear anywhere in the supplement or in any repository I could reach.

a1_downloadable.note: The only deposited dataset, SRA BioProject PRJNA1379557, is not public: NCBI BioProject esearch, SRA esearch and ENA all return zero records and the BioProject page errors (checked 2026-10-16). The supplement contains no spacer-position tables, no bedgraph tracks and no code link, so the quantitative data behind every figure is unavailable.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: For the obvious project (predict where along a phage genome a type III system grabs a spacer), the label is a per-position spacer count that exists only as bedgraph tracks the authors did not deposit; it would have to be rebuilt from raw amplicon reads that are themselves unavailable. The 182 supplement spacers do carry a hand-written 'Early/Middle/Late - OrfNN' annotation, which is a column, but it is a coarse manual gene label, not the measured acquisition frequency.

a3_inputs_present.note: Spacer sequences (30-41 nucleotides) and 8-nucleotide flanking sequences are literally written out in the Word tables, and phage 2972 plus the 752 Streptococcus phage genomes are public at NCBI, so inputs would be obtainable.

a4_units_stated.note: Growth-curve file states OD600 (optical density at 600 nanometres) versus time in hours; the paper states SPM (spacers per million) for the undeposited tracks. Checked in the Excel file.

a5_enough_rows.note: Counted in the files: 182 BIM spacers total (130 type III-A, 52 type II-A), 37 escaper rows, 39 strains with growth curves. Far below the ~1,500-row bar, and below the ~400-row classification bar.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Entire available supplement is 4.5 MB; it fits trivially. This is the only Part A item that is comfortably satisfied.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: The paper says 125 BIMs with early-gene spacers out of the type III set; the type III table has 130 rows, consistent with 2 middle and 3 late plus 125 early. No contradiction found.

a8_label_provenance.note: The 'Early / Middle / Late' class attached to each spacer is an annotation transferred from a previous RNA-sequencing study of phage 2972 and from gene-order heuristics, not a measurement made on these spacers; and it is largely determined by genome position, which is also the feature. Predicting it from sequence position would be close to circular.

honest_claim_h3: No claim is supportable: the measured quantity (how often each phage genome position is captured as a spacer) was never released, and the 182 spacers that are released are too few and too coarsely labelled to support any model.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use phage DNA sequence around each position to predict how often a bacterial immune system copies that position into its memory.
plain_idea.train_on: Positions along Streptococcus phage genomes, each with its local DNA sequence, promoter context and transcription level. The number of usable examples is unknown because the per-position spacer counts were never deposited; only 182 individual spacer sequences are public.
plain_idea.predict: How many spacers a type III-A CRISPR system acquires at that position, measured by amplicon sequencing of expanded CRISPR arrays and normalised as spacers per million. That measurement exists only as undeposited bedgraph tracks.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Groups engineering CRISPR recording devices and phage-resistant starter cultures want to know which part of an invading genome gets remembered; a sequence model of acquisition bias would let them design or avoid hotspots.

label_elsewhere.sources: Not applicable for a reject; spacer-acquisition frequency per genome position is not a label held by any public resource I know of, and I did not find one in search.
label_elsewhere.why: Nothing outside this paper measures how often a given phage position becomes a spacer, so there is no external training or validation set.

ml_idea: Dead as proposed: predict per-position type III-A CRISPR spacer acquisition frequency along phage genomes from local DNA sequence and transcription context, with a DNA language model such as Nucleotide Transformer frozen and a regression head on top. It needs the per-position spacer depth tracks, which were not deposited. If the authors release PRJNA1379557 and the bedgraphs, revisit: the biology (acquisition follows early transcription) is a genuinely unmodelled sequence-to-phenotype mapping.

effort.compute_note: Only the 4.5 MB supplement is available, so laptop feasibility is irrelevant; no timing was done because there is no dataset to time.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Query NCBI and ENA for BioProject PRJNA1379557 — it took one minute and returned nothing, which killed the project.

verdict_reason: Part A1 fails: the only deposited data, SRA BioProject PRJNA1379557, is not public on NCBI or ENA as of 2026-10-16, and the supplement contains no spacer-position tables or tracks. A5 and A8 fail too — the public part is 182 hand-annotated spacer sequences and 39 growth curves, and their Early/Middle/Late label is an annotation carried over from an earlier RNA-sequencing study rather than a measurement on these spacers. Worth re-checking in a few months if the BioProject is released.
